newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen earnings disappoint, stock rises.
newsitem.headline: Loewen earnings disappoint, stock rises.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc reported fourth-quarter earnings that fell modestly short of analysts' expectations on Wednesday, but its stock rose after being pounded recently by fears of an even worse performance.
Loewen shares climbed 3/4 to 33-1/4 in New York and 0.80 to 45.50 in Toronto.

The funeral home and cemetery operator earlier said its fourth-quarter earnings were US$0.36 a share before costs associated with fighting a hostile takeover bid by Service Corp International. Including those costs, it earned US$0.13 a share, up from a US$2.35 loss a year ago.
After recently scaling back their forecasts, most analysts had expected earnings of US$0.37 to US$0.39 a share before the takeover costs and net earnings of US$0.17 to US$0.21 a share.

Raymond James analyst Susan Little said a preliminary review of the fourth-quarter results pointed to higher than expected ongoing costs and greater takeover-related expenses. "It looks like the G&A was higher than was expected and the charges after tax were also higher," she said.
Analysts and traders attributed the rise in the stock price to a recovery after heavy selling pushed it as low as 31 in New York in recent days.
"We're seeing a little rebound," said one trader.

Investors took heart from Loewen's upbeat assessment of its growth prospects for the year, and the share price advance appeared to be a case of selling on rumor and buying on the news, another trader added.

The company's stock came under heavy selling recently amid a swirl of confusing rumors about a potential accounting problem and a looming earnings disappointment. Loewen said the speculation was unfounded.

Despite the stock gain, analysts said Loewen was unlikely to achieve 1997 earnings per share in the US$1.70 range, a level with which the company previously said it was comfortable. Analysts now seemed to be gravitating toward figures closer to US$1.60.
One industry source reported speculation that Loewen might withdraw a lawsuit filed against Service Corp as part of its takeover defense. If so, that could reduce the company's legal costs in 1997.
